papers.title: SERS of Bottled Water: Automated PET Nanoplastic Detection and Quantification.
papers.abstract: Nanoplastics represent an emerging contaminant of growing environmental and public health concern, with polyethylene terephthalate (PET) being on topic due to its dominant use in beverage packaging. This study presents a SERS approach for the detection and quantification of PET nanoplastics in commercial bottled water, combining SERS with colloidal silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) and commercial solid SERS substrates, with automated Pearson correlation spectral classification. Mapping SERS samples of PET-bottled water combined with a Python identification algorithm enabled the detection of PET nanoplastics, while SEM-EDX analysis confirmed the presence of nanoscale carbon-oxygen particles consistent with PET stoichiometry. Beyond PET, phthalocyanine pigment nanoparticles, likely originating from bottle package, and inorganic residues including calcite, gypsum, and sodium nitrate were simultaneously identified, demonstrating the multianalyte capability of the approach. Using colloidal AgNPs, the estimated PET nanoplastic concentration was 17.25 ± 1.6 million particles per 0.5 L bottle (34.5 ± 3.2 million particles/L), comparative with values reported by nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA) and stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy in comparable studies. The method requires minimal sample preparation, limited to concentration by evaporation, without digestion or extraction steps, and preliminary results can be obtained within a few hours. These findings establish SERS combined with automated spectral analysis as a practical and sensitive screening tool for nanoplastic monitoring in drinking water, reporting particle concentrations directly in the number of particles per liter and with potential applicability to broader water quality analysis.

papers.title: Atypical Atrial Flutter From Lipomatous Hypertrophy of the Interatrial Septum in a Procedure-Naive Patient.
papers.abstract: Lipomatous hypertrophy of the interatrial septum (LHIS) is generally benign and often discovered incidentally; however, it can occasionally serve as a substrate for atrial arrhythmias. An 86-year-old man with no prior cardiac history presented with new onset atrial flutter (AFL) with an atrial rate of 280 beats/min. During an electrophysiology study, intracardiac echocardiography identified LHIS. Three-dimensional electroanatomic activation mapping demonstrated the earliest focal activation at the superior posteroseptal right atrium, corresponding to the location of the LHIS. Radiofrequency ablation at this site terminated the AFL, rendering the tachycardia noninducible. LHIS can act as an isolated arrhythmogenic substrate for atypical AFL. The combination of intracardiac echocardiography and high-density electroanatomic mapping allows precise localization of the arrhythmogenic focus, facilitating safe and effective catheter ablation. LHIS should be considered a potential arrhythmogenic substrate in patients with atypical AFL. Catheter ablation of LHIS-associated AFL is safe and effective.

papers.title: Prolactin Receptor Long Isoform ΔS1 Expression is Reduced in the Dorsal Root Ganglia of Humans with Chronic Pain
papers.abstract: Prolactin receptor (PRLR) isoforms, specifically the short (PRLR-S) and long (PRLR-L), are differentially expressed in pathological conditions and may be involved in the induction and maintenance of pain in females. PRLR sex-dependent actions are well studied in rodent models of chronic pain, but the translatability of these findings have only been assessed in electrophysiology studies that found consistent results with previous sex differences described in mice. To increase our understanding of the sexual dimorphic nature of prolactin actions on sensory neurons and our knowledge of how this body of work applies to the human nervous system, we characterized the expression of the short and long isoforms of PRLR with RNAscope in situ hybridization in human dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons. Based on data in mice, we hypothesized PRLR-S and PRLR-L would be equally expressed in human DRG neurons, with higher expression in females. To test this, we used DRG tissues recovered from male and female organ donors and cervix as a positive control. Our results demonstrated human DRG neurons express more PRLR-L, specifically transcript variant 6 ({Delta}S1), than PRLR-S in both sexes and that female donors had a higher expression of PRLR overall. In DRGs from female organ donors with a history of chronic pain we observed less PRLR-L expression, a finding consistent with previous studies in pain models in female mice. Expression for both PRLR isoforms in cervix was consistent with previous reports. An analysis of previously published RNA sequencing studies on human DRGs revealed that PRLR expression is confined mostly to TRPV1-positive nociceptors in humans, consistent with our RNAscope-based findings. We conclude that the PRLR-L ({Delta}S1) form is the major isoform expressed in human DRG neurons, that this expression is higher in females than in males, and that PRLR-L ({Delta}S1) expression is suppressed in chronic pain conditions in females.
